compound.name: herniarin (7-methoxycoumarin)
compound.one_liner: Simple coumarin of chamomile flower (with umbelliferone 0.01-0.08 %); not an anticoagulant coumarin.

occurrences.source_citation: EMA/HMPC. Assessment report on Matricaria recutita L., flos and Matricaria recutita L., aetheroleum. EMA/HMPC/55837/2011 (7 Jul 2015). https://www.ema.europa.eu/en/documents/herbal-report/final-assessment-report-matricaria-recutita-l-flos-and-matricaria-recutita-l-aetheroleum-first-version_en.pdf-0
occurrences.database: Dr. Duke's Phytochemical and Ethnobotanical Databases
occurrences.note: Duke: HERNIARIN Flower 320-915 ppm. | Basis as recorded: % of flower; range given for herniarin and umbelliferone together Basis (fresh/dry weight) not stated by the source; excluded from /compare until confirmed.

pharmacology.functional_notes: EMA gives no anticoagulant warning for these coumarins [10].

compound.teaching_note: 'Contains coumarins' does not mean 'thins blood': herniarin is a 7-methoxycoumarin, not a 4-hydroxycoumarin like warfarin (structural comparison). A chamomile-warfarin bleeding case exists, but its mechanism is a proposal [48].
gaps: Anticoagulant activity of herniarin not researched; structural argument only.
No human evidence for the isolated compound found in this pass.
